input: Write a eulogy for my grandfather's memorial

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The eulogy's length and depth depends on whether it should be a brief tribute or a full speech covering his whole life story.
The tone and content changes significantly depending on who is delivering it — the user themselves, a family member, or someone else — and who the audience is.
The setting (religious ceremony, casual gathering, graveside service) shapes the appropriate register, formality, and any spiritual references.
A time limit for the eulogy directly caps how much content can be included and determines pacing.
Knowing whether the tone should lean toward heartfelt and solemn, celebratory and uplifting, or include humour determines the entire emotional arc of the piece.
Understanding what the user most wants the audience to walk away feeling or remembering about the grandfather defines what 'done well' looks like.
Specific memories, anecdotes, or facts about the grandfather are the raw material without which the eulogy will be generic rather than personal.

gold.taskTitle: Write a eulogy for grandfather's memorial
gold.taskDescription: Write a eulogy to be delivered at the user's grandfather's memorial service.

questions.title: How long should the eulogy be when spoken aloud?
questions.description: Establish a target duration (e.g., 2 minutes, 5 minutes, 10 minutes) to set the appropriate word count and scope of content.

questions.title: Who will be delivering the eulogy at the service?
questions.description: Identify whether the user is speaking themselves or writing it for someone else, as this affects voice, personal pronouns, and relationship framing.

questions.title: What is the setting and format of the memorial service?
questions.description: Determine whether it is a religious ceremony, a funeral home service, a graveside gathering, or an informal celebration of life, to calibrate formality and any spiritual language.

questions.title: What overall tone should the eulogy carry throughout?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a solemn and heartfelt tribute, a warm celebration of life, a tone that includes gentle humour, or a blend.

questions.title: What specific memories or stories should be included?
questions.description: Gather key anecdotes, defining moments, passions, or phrases associated with the grandfather that will make the eulogy personal and vivid.

questions.title: What aspects of his life or character must the eulogy cover?
questions.description: Determine the non-negotiable elements — career, family role, hobbies, values, achievements — versus what can be left out to keep focus.

questions.title: What feeling should the audience be left with at the end?
questions.description: Define the emotional destination — comfort, inspiration, gratitude, celebration — so the closing of the eulogy lands with the right impact.
